Subject: Questions on hosted API residency & subprocessors (DPA)

Hannah / Marissa —

Thanks for the quick DPA draft. A couple of items legal flagged that we need clarified before we share with procurement: 

1) Data residency language: the draft says "customers may request region-specific hosting" but doesn't say what guarantees or controls exist in the hosted product (console toggles, where artifacts live, how backups are handled). Can you provide a plain-language snippet we can include in the SOW?

2) Subprocessors: we need a clear, customer-facing explanation of how the subprocessor list is published and updated. Specifically: 
  - Where in the console can we see the live list? 
  - Will customers be notified of changes and how (email / console banner)? 
  - Is there a CSV export or machine-readable feed we can ingest for our inventory?

3) Cross-border transfers: is the standard transfer mechanism SCCs? Is there a data transfer assessment for the hosted API traffic?

I've attached our redlines and a short spreadsheet of questions. Happy to hop on a 30-minute call if that's easier.

Attached: GreenLeaf_DPA_questions.xlsx

Best,
Priya Shah
Head of Privacy & Compliance
GreenLeaf Health

Draft plain-language snippet for console + DPA (attached as plain_language_subprocessors.md). Two things I focused on: clarity for procurement, and operational steps for customers. Suggestions below — feel free to edit for tone/length.

Console snippet (short):
- "Subprocessor directory: View the current list of subprocessors at Console > Security > Subprocessors. The directory is updated in real time; a timestamp and change log are shown for each entry. Exports: CSV and API endpoints are available for customer inventories."

Notification + cadence (short):
- "When we add or change a subprocessor that materially affects processing, customers with affected contracts receive an email and a console notification at least 30 days before the change takes effect. Non-material changes are posted to the change log and highlighted in the directory."

Data residency / hosting (short):

Priya / Daniel —

Appreciate the patience while we pulled this together. Below is a consolidated, customer-facing summary you can include in the SOW or share with procurement. I've included links and attachments for the export/map we referenced.

Proposed plain-language summary (for SOW / Console help):
"Redwood hosted customers can select region-specific hosting for API traffic and stored artifacts (US, EU, APAC). For customers who contract for a region, we keep data at rest and backups in the selected region. Cross-border transfers that are required for operational continuity rely on EU Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) or equivalent mechanisms; we maintain documented transfer assessments. Subprocessors are published in the Console (Security > Subprocessors) with a visible change log and timestamp. Customers may export the current list as CSV or access it via the Subprocessors API; significant changes that materially affect processing will be emailed to affected customers at least 30 days prior to the change."

What we can provide now:
- A console link showing the live subprocessor map: https://repl.redwood.com/subprocessors/map?id=rl-23
- CSV export: redwood_subprocessor_map_v2.csv (attached)
- Short residency snippet file (attached): redwood_hosted-residency-snippet.txt

Open items we are confirming (will follow up separately):
- Exact location of backup snapshots for hosted domains (Vivek to confirm whether snapshots are stored regionally for all hosted tiers).
- Whether automated console export exists for self-serve customers vs. partner-managed accounts (Vivek).

If that wording works for you, we can update the DPA exhibit and the Console help copy. Happy to jump on the Monday 11:00 PT call if you'd like to walk through live.

Best,
